summary: Postgres date-integer subtraction with an untyped bound parameter resolves the wrong operator overload
evidence: sql`${today}::date - ${skipRecentDays}` (skipRecentDays a plain JS number, no cast) raised 'operator does not exist: date >= integer' from every randomizer.db.test.ts test touching the default recency filter. Reproduced directly against pg (bypassing Kysely) with an untyped $2 param in 'date >= $1::date - $2': Postgres resolves $2 via the date-date->integer overload instead of date-integer->date, so the whole subtraction becomes an integer and the outer >= comparison has no operator. Casting the parameter explicitly (${skipRecentDays}::int) fixes it; verified with the same bypass script before and after.
